newsitem.title: ROMANIA: FOCUS-Romanian leu slides, dollar in demand.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Romanian leu slides, dollar in demand.

text.p: Romania's leu, stable for months after the government liberalised currency markets, slid sharply against the dollar on Thursday and traders said the fall was partly caused by profit-taking on equity markets.
The leu closed at 7,400/500 from Wednesday's 7,200/270, a fall of more than 2.5 percent, as demand for dollars surged for the first time in a month.

"There were some foreign investors who tried to change leu returns from equity trading into dollars," said a dealer with a foreign bank in Bucharest. "But I did not see orders to transfer that money abroad."

Both Romania's bourse, in operation for the past 18 months, and the more recently opened over-the-counter market, turned bearish this week after weeks of upward trend. Brokers said investors saw opportunities for profit-taking as some stocks had become expensive.
Other traders said Thursday's quicker decline came as a correction after a relatively long flat period and was fuelled by a parallel plunge in money market rates.
Short-term rates have sunk to 20 percent from about 50 percent a week ago on a market flooded with leu funds after the central bank (BNR) proceeded with long-term dollar purchases.
But BNR officials said the currency market, generally unresponsive to outside influences, had reacted to the dollar's strength in the international markets in the past few days.
"Our market finally digested the recent moves of the U.S. currency on the international markets," BNR communication manager Adrian Vasilescu told Reuters, without elaborating.
Dealers said the local market was rather slow to react to international moves. "In theory, it might be true but our market is rather dictated by demand and supply here," said one.
Romania's centrist government, elected last November, has proceeded with reforms long delayed under the previous leftist administration, including the freeing of currency markets.
Legislation appealing to foreign investors has drawn in large sums of hard currency in the past months, channelled particularly into Romania's fledgling equities markets.
The BNR had for weeks been making large dollar purchases to prevent the leu from firming and hurting exporters.
Most traders were reluctant to say whether pressure on the leu would continue. "Such big (dollar-buying) orders might be a temporary development," said one dealer.

The money market remained fairly liquid on Thursday with short-term rates hovering at about 15-20 percent amid smooth trading after the BNR mopped up some leu funds to prevent prices from falling further.
"The BNR was on the leu side taking deposits," said one trader with a state-run bank, adding that the BNR paid in a range of 25 to 30 percent.
